context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: The route `app.get('/api/Users', security.isAuthorized())` only checks that the caller is logged in, so any authenticated user can list every user's Personal Data. Add a server-side role check after authentication, for example `app.get('/api/Users', security.isAuthorized(), security.hasRole('admin'))`. Build `hasRole` from the role in the verified JWT (`security.authenticatedUsers.from(req).data.role`) and return 403 when the role doesn't match. Never take the role or user id from the path, query or body. Put the same middleware chain on every method of the route with `app.all('/api/Users', ...)` or `app.route('/api/Users').all(security.isAuthorized(), security.hasRole('admin'))`, and the same rule on `/api/Users/:id`. For `/api/Users/:id`, allow access only if the requester is an admin or `req.params.id === String(authenticatedUser.data.id)`. Regular users who need their own record should use a self-scoped endpoint such as `/rest/user/whoami`, which reads the user id from the token. Also strip sensitive fields (password hash, totpSecret, deluxeToken) from responses with a finale/Sequelize `attributes.exclude` or an after-read hook. Then confirm that a non-admin token gets 403 on GET/POST/PUT/DELETE for `/api/Users` and on other users' `/api/Users/:id`, and that admin access still works.
